findings.title: Cleanup ticker silently changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute
findings.body: The ticker interval for the whole cleanup service is changed from 10 minutes to 1 minute. Nothing in the PR description mentions this, and it is unrelated to the annotation deadlock fix. It increases how often every cleanup job runs (snapshots, dashboard versions, images, invites, short URLs, query history, annotations) by 10x. This looks like a leftover debugging change and should be reverted or justified separately.

findings.title: Per-batch cleanup logs at Error level and dump full ID lists
findings.body: CleanAnnotations logs every batch with r.log.Error, including the entire slice of IDs ("ids", ids) and the SQL condition. Batches can be up to AnnotationCleanupJobBatchSize (default and max in tests is 32767) and the loop runs until no rows remain, so a single cleanup run can emit many error-level log lines with large ID lists. Success paths are not errors, so this floods error logs and inflates log volume on every cleanup cycle. The same pattern is used at lines 536-537, 554-557 and in CleanOrphanedAnnotationTags (576-579). These should be Debug logs without the ID list.

findings.title: Logged 'err' field is always nil in the batch log lines
findings.body: The log calls after the batch use "err", y where y is the deleteByIDs error, but the line at 534 logs "err", err from fetchIDs, which is always nil at that point because errors return early. Logging err=nil on success is harmless but the field is misleading. It is not needed on the success path since errors are already returned to the caller.

findings.title: Quadratic string building for SQLite inline ID list
findings.body: The SQLite branch builds the IN-list with values = fmt.Sprintf("%s, %d", values, v) inside a loop. Each iteration copies the whole accumulated string, so building a list of up to 32767 IDs is O(n^2) in bytes copied, on every batch. Using strings.Builder or strconv.AppendInt would avoid this. The IDs are int64 from the database, so there is no injection risk here.

findings.title: Cleanup of inserted rows is registered after the inserts and assertions that can fail
findings.body: createTestAnnotations and the count assertions run before t.Cleanup is registered for each subtest. If any of those assertions fail (require calls call t.FailNow), the annotation and annotation_tag rows are left in the shared fakeSQL database and subsequent subtests start with unexpected data, producing misleading follow-on failures. The cleanup registration should come before the inserts.
